end.note: Ends at the LHC-wide start of Long Shutdown 3 (June 2026); mirrors experiment:lhcf.
CERN schedule: the LHC resumes operation in mid-2030; the rest of the CERN complex restarts in stages from mid-2028.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3
intervals.locator: home.cern/science/long-shutdown-3, item of 5 August 2026 "The LHC is being warmed up from near absolute zero to room temperature"
intervals.note: The detector record carries the same Long Shutdown 3 interval as experiment:lhcf, whose interval note gives the evidence and CERN's wording for the bounds; the state is inferred from the LHC being shut down.
intervals.quote: Following its final physics run, the accelerator has been switched off to begin CERN’s Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) ... The HiLumi LHC, scheduled to begin operation in 2030

name: LHCf detector
notes: home.cern gives detector mass (40 kg) and dimensions (30 cm × 80 cm × 10 cm) per arm as of a November 2012 page snapshot; recorded in specs below.

placements.locator: INSPIRE experiment record 1126263, field description; home.cern LHCf page corroborates IP1
placements.note: LHCf's two arms are physically in the TAN neutral-particle absorbers ±140 m from IP1, not in the ATLAS cavern itself; the detector is placed at the existing site:cern-point-1-atlas.
placements.quote: installed at zero degree collision angle +-140m from an interaction point (IP)

total_mass.locator: home.cern LHCf page (as of a November 2012 snapshot)
total_mass.quote: Each of the two detectors weighs only 40 kilograms and measures 30 cm long by 80 cm high and 10 cm wide.

summary.plain: Two small, 40-kilogram detectors placed 140 metres either side of the ATLAS collision point, catching particles thrown almost exactly along the beam direction.
summary.technical: Two identical imaging sampling calorimeters (Arm1, Arm2), tungsten/scintillator/position-sensitive-sensor construction, each ~40 kg, 30 cm × 80 cm × 10 cm, at zero-degree collision angle ±140 m from IP1.

technology.quote: Two LHCf detectors, consisting of imaging calorimeters made of tungsten plates, plastic scintillator and position sensitive sensors, are installed at zero degree collision angle +-140m from an interaction point (IP).
technology.value: two compact imaging sampling calorimeters (tungsten plates, plastic scintillator, position-sensitive sensors)
